rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters worshiped idols as means of drawing near to God, since a rational person would not think lifeless stone independently benefits or harms; commoners' beliefs vary without limit.
rows.anchor: القوم عبدوا الأصنام تقربا إلى الله، فيبعد أن يعتقد عاقل أن الحجر والجماد ينفع ويضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that the idolaters believed their idols themselves could bring benefit and harm.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اعتقدوا فيها النفع والضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation in truth means God created for truth rather than falsehood, contrary to determinists who attribute every falsehood to God's creation, will, and decree.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد بخلقه الحق، ولم يرد الباطل، خلاف قول أهل الجبر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وعاصم وحمزة ويعقوب وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read the pronoun in yرضه with a shortened, lightly pronounced damma, preserving the original form while easing pronunciation.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وعاصم وحمزة ويعقوب وأبو عمرو بضم الهاء مختلسة غير مشبعة للتخفيف والدلالة على الأصل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: In some transmissions they read yرضه with a silent hāʾ for ease of pronunciation.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب في بعض الروايات عنهما: يرضه ساكنة الهاء بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وابن كثير والكسائي ونافع
rows.claim: In some transmissions they lengthen the damma on the hāʾ, retaining the original form; a similar reading is also reported from Ibn Amr and Abu Bakr from Asim.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وابن كثير والكسائي ونافع في بعض الروايات مضمومة الهاء مشبعة، وروي نحوه عن ابن عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An imperative is literally a speaker's directive to someone lower in rank, with the speaker intending the act; applying it to oneself is impossible, and its use for action is figurative.
rows.anchor: الأمر: قول القائل لمن دونه: (افعل) إذا كان مريدا للمأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imperative forms can instead convey threat, permission, guidance, or similar meanings.
rows.anchor: وقد ترد صيغة الأمر فلا تكون أمرا بأن تكون تهديدا أو إباحة أو إرشادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn can mean obedience, recompense, the religion one follows, or customary practice.
rows.anchor: والدين: الطاعة، والدين: الجزاء، والدين: ما يدان به، والدين: العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincerity in religion means acting for God without admixture.
rows.anchor: والإخلاص في الدين: أن يعمله لله تعالى من غير شائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A zullah is a high covering; calling the punishment's canopies zullah is figurative and expansive, by analogy with the canopies of Paradise.
rows.anchor: والظلة: الستر العالي، وجمعه: ظلل، وقيل: الظلة في العذاب مجاز وتوسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Threatening, intimidation, and warning are near synonyms, while encouragement is the opposite of intimidation.
rows.anchor: والتخويف والترهيب والتحذير نظائر، ونقيض الترهيب: الترغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says these verses were revealed when people invited the Messenger to follow his forefathers' religion.
rows.anchor: قيل: لما دعوا رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وآله - إلى دين الآباء نزلت هذه الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhull means the opposite of honor and is synonymous with disgrace.
rows.anchor: الذل: نقيض العز، ونظيره: الهوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A maljaʾ is a place to which one flees for refuge.
rows.anchor: والملجأ: ما يلتجأ إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāshiʿīn is accusative as a circumstantial expression describing their state of humility.
rows.anchor: خاشعين نصبا على الحال، أي: في حال الخشوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahylihim is the object of khasirū; this yāʾ does not take fatḥa.
rows.anchor: أهليهم نصب ب (خسروا)، إلا أن هذه الياء لا يدخلها الفتح

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Min in min taraf can mean bi, giving the sense of looking with a furtive eye.
rows.anchor: قيل: (من) بمعنى الباء أي: بطرف خفي، عن يونس

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-ṭaraf means the eye itself.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: الطرف: العين، أي: من عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhīna may be nominative as a resumed subject, or the predicate of inna.
rows.anchor: الذين في موضع رفع، على تقدير: هم الذين خسروا، وقيل: خبر (إن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's leading astray here is explained either as justly punishing and destroying someone at Judgment, or as turning that person away from mercy and Paradise; the second is attributed to Abu Ali.
rows.anchor: قيل: يعذبه ويهلكه يوم القيامة لاستحقاقه ذلك، وقيل: يضله عن رحمته وجنته، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one misled has no protecting ally besides God to ward off punishment.
rows.anchor: فما له من ولي ناصر يمنع العذاب منه من بعده أي: سوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned ask whether a path back to worldly life remains so they can make up their failures with righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: هل إلى رجعة إلى الدنيا طريق؛ لنتلافى ما فرطنا بالأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in tarāhum may be to Muhammad, to any listener, or to any person.
rows.anchor: وتراهم يا محمد، وقيل: أيها السامع، أو أيها الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned face the Fire in abasement, submission, and regret.
rows.anchor: يعرضون عليها أي: على النار خاشعين أي: خاضعين متواضعين نادمين من الذل والهوان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Looking with a furtive eye means looking in a humiliated, abject manner.
rows.anchor: من عين خفي قيل: ذليل، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والسدي والقرظي
rows.claim: The condemned steal glances toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: يسارقون النظر، عن الحسن، وقتادة، والسدي، والقرظي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are that only part of the eye opens because of the terror, that the blind see the Fire with their hearts, or that they lower their eyes when it appears.
rows.anchor: لا تفتح كلها، وإنما ينظر ببعضها إلى النار لعظم ما فيها من العذاب والأهوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers call them true losers because they squandered their souls, forfeiting Paradise and bringing punishment upon themselves.
rows.anchor: رأس المال هو النفس، فإذا أوبقها فلا خسران أعظم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lost family is variously understood as spouses, children, and kin; houris; or the family they would have had in Paradise if they had believed.
rows.anchor: أزواجه، وأولاده، وأقاربه، لا ينتفع بهم، وقيل: أهله من الحور العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that wrongdoers remain in punishment may finish the believers' speech or begin a new statement from God.
rows.anchor: قيل: هذا تمام كلام المؤمنين، وقيل: بل هو خبر مبتدأ من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned have no ally or helper who can rescue them from punishment.
rows.anchor: أي: لا ولي لهم، ولا ناصر يتولى تخليصهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final denial of a path answers their question about return: one destroyed by God has no route to salvation; one distanced from Paradise has no guide to it; alternatively every good path is shut.
rows.anchor: من أهلكه الله فما له من طريق إلى النجاة، وقيل: من أبعده الله من الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
rows.claim: They treat the bāʾ in the common reading bi-qādir as an added particle, comparing it to the bāʾ in tanbutu bi-d-duhn.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو عبيدة والأخفش: صلة، كقوله: (تنبت بالدهن)

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: They explain the bāʾ as entering the predicate in response to a negation, as in laysa Zayd bi-qāʾim.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي والفراء: دخلت في جواب النفي، كقولهم: ليس زيد بقائم

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub reads the phrase as the verb yaqdir, without alif; several early readers also used this form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب: يقدر بالياء وبغير ألف على الفعل

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim prefers the verb reading because using bāʾ in the predicate of anna is weak.
rows.anchor: واختاره أبو حاتم؛ لأن دخول الباء في خبر (أن) ضعيف

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda prefers the common nominal reading because the reciters agree on it and Ibn Masud's reading has qādir without bāʾ.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيدة قراءة العامة لإجماع القراء، ولأنها في قراءة ابن مسعود (قادر) بغير باء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Response means that one's actions answer the caller's summons; dāʿī Allāh is the one who calls people to obedience, and supplication, asking, and requesting are synonymous.
rows.anchor: الإجابة: موافقة العمل لدعاء الداعي لأجله، أجاب فهو مجيب، وداعي الله: من يدعو إلى طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijāra is securing someone against fear; a walī is one who takes responsibility for helping when needed.
rows.anchor: والإجارة: أن تؤمنه من خوف، يقال: أجاره يجيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿyā in walking describes difficulty or inability, while ʿayya describes being unable to speak; a chronic, incurable condition is called dāʾ ʿiyāʾ.
rows.anchor: أعيا الرجل في مشيته يعيا إعياء: إذا شق عليه أو امتنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resolve is a firm commitment in the heart; ʿazama ʿalayka can mean I adjure you, or I command you emphatically.
rows.anchor: والعزم: عقد القلب على شيء أن يفعله، ونحوه: العزيمة، قال ابن زيد: عزمت عليك: أقسمت عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resolve can also mean obligations, strength and patience, or preparation; deliberation prepares for an affair while resolve carries it through.
rows.anchor: والعزائم: الفرائض، والعزم: القوة على الشيء والصبر عليه، وقيل: الحزم التأهب للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resolve is a particular kind of will, not a separate faculty from will.
rows.anchor: والعزم: إرادة مخصوصة، وليس بمعنى سوى الإرادة

rows.speaker: الحسن والأعرج وعاصم وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read adbar al-sujūd with fatḥa on the first alif, treating adbār as a plural of dabr.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن والأعرج وعاصم وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب: وأدبار السجود بفتح الألف

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس
rows.claim: They read the first vowel as kasra, taking idbār as the verbal noun of adbara.
rows.anchor: والفتح جمع دبر. قراءة العامة: فنقبوا بفتح القاف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan also read fa-naqabū with a light, undoubled qāf.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن بفتحها فنقبوا مخففة

rows.speaker: السلمي ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: They read fa-naqqibū with a doubled qāf and kasra as a threatening imperative: travel through the lands and see whether escape is possible.
rows.anchor: وعن السلمي ويحيى بن يعمر بكسرها مشددة على التهديد والوعيد أي: طوفوا في البلاد هل تجدون محيصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṭsh is forceful seizing, and naqib is a path; its root concerns opening a passage for travel.
rows.anchor: البطش: الأخذ بشدة، ومنه: (إن بطش ربك لشديد). والنقب: الطريق

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line uses āfāq to support the sense of traveling the routes and passes of a region.
rows.anchor: وقول امرئ القيس: لقد طوفت في الآفاق حتى ... رضيت من الغنيمة بالإياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A naqīb is a leader who knows his people's routes and affairs; a niqāb is a pass between two mountains.
rows.anchor: ومنه: نقيب القوم كالأمير؛ لأنه يعرف طرق أمورهم، والنقاب الطريق بين جبلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying about the plague uses niqāb for an entrance or pass of Medina.
rows.anchor: ومنه حديث النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لما كثر حديث الطاعون: أرجو ألا يطلع إلينا نقابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥayyiṣ means a route of escape or turning aside to flee.
rows.anchor: والمحيص: المحيد، وهو الذهاب في ناحية الهرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lughūb means exhaustion; the verb laghiba allows either fatḥa or ḍamma on its middle consonant.
rows.anchor: واللغوب: الإعياء، لغب يلغب بفتح الغين وضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kam ahlaknā is formally a question used for emphasis; kam indicates abundance, the opposite of fewness.
rows.anchor: كم أهلكنا استفهام، والمراد التقرير، و(كم) للتكثير نقيض التقليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min may precede the counted noun after kam because in a report kam functions like the number with a genitive complement, as in ten garments or ten of the garments.
rows.anchor: لأنها في الخبر بمنزلة العدد نفسه بالمضاف، كقوله: عشرة أثواب وعشرة من الأثواب

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read mawqiʿ in the singular, intending the collective class of star-settings.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: بموقع النجوم بغير ألف على الواحد، وأراد الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the plural mawāqiʿ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بمواقع على الجمع

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمرو
rows.claim: Isa ibn Amr reads fa-la-uqsim with a clearly articulated oath form.
rows.anchor: وعن عيسى بن عمرو: فلأقسم على تحقيق القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasam means an oath and derives from qasāma; mawqiʿ is the place where something falls or occurs.
rows.anchor: القسم: اليمين، أخذ من القسامة. والموقع: موضع الوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karīm describes something whose nature is to be honored; tanzīl is a verbal noun used by extension to describe what is revealed.
rows.anchor: والكريم: الذي من شأنه أن يكرم. والتنزيل: مصدر نزله تنزيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech is an accident that does not persist; it descends from its locus or from the locus of its sign.
rows.anchor: والكلام: عرض لا يبقى، وإنما ينزل من محله أو محل أمارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mudhin is one who smoothly and quickly goes along with falsehood contrary to what is outwardly apparent, like oil's easy flow.
rows.anchor: والمدهن: الذي يجري في الباطل على خلاف الظاهر، كالدهن في سهولة ذلك والإسراع فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report places the rebuke for attributing provision to stars in the context of asking for rain.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون) في الاستسقاء، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says a servant loses if his only share of God's Book is denying it.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: خسر عبد لا يكون حظه من كتاب الله إلا التكذيب به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When rain fell during the Prophet's time, people differed: some called it God's mercy, while others credited a particular star; the verses were then revealed.
rows.anchor: مطر الناس على عهد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال: أصبح من الناس شاكر ومنهم كافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that on a journey the Companions lacked water; after the Prophet prayed and supplicated, they received rain, and he heard a man credit a star, prompting revelation.
rows.anchor: فصلى ركعتين، ودعا الله تعالى، فسقوا، ثم ركب، فمر برجل يغترف، ويقول: مطرنا بنوء كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawlā can mean awlā, the one more entitled or liable; Labid's verse pictures each side as more exposed to danger.
rows.anchor: مولى المخافة خلفها وأمامها أي: يحسب أن كليهما أولى بالمخافة

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid's line uses mawlā with the sense of awlā, the more fitting one to fear.
rows.anchor: مولى المخافة خلفها وأمامها أي: يحسب أن كليهما أولى بالمخافة

rows.speaker: نافع وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read mā nuzzila with a light zāy, from the simple verb nazala.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وحفص عن عاصم: وما نزل خفيفة الزاي من نزل ينزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers double the zāy, reading the intensive verb nazzala.
rows.anchor: الباقون: نزل مشددة الزاي من نزل تنزيلا

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub reads the clause in the second person as a prohibition: wa-lā takūnū.
rows.anchor: قرأ. يعقوب: ولا تكونوا على الخطاب والنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the third person, wa-lā yakūnū.
rows.anchor: والقراء بالياء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read al-muṣaddiqīn with a light ṣād, meaning those who affirm God and His Messenger, that is, believers.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو بكر عن عاصم: [المصدقين والمصدقات] بتخفيف الصاد من التصديق

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: They prefer the doubled ṣād reading for those who give charity, noting that Ubayy's reading explicitly says al-mutasaddiqīn.
rows.anchor: واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم، قالا في قراءة أبي: (إن المتصدقين والمتصدقات)

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: A'mash adds a final hāʾ to yuḍāʿif and reads the ʿayn with kasra.
rows.anchor: وعن الأعمش: يضاعفه بكسر العين وزيادة هاء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read yuḍaʿʿif without alif, while the remaining readers read yuḍāʿif with alif.
rows.anchor: ثم اختلفوا، فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وابن عامر: يضعف بغير ألف، الباقون بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anā means has the time come, from anā yaʾnī, and is used of something reaching its appointed time.
rows.anchor: ألم يأن: ألم يحن، [أنى يأني] إنا: إذا حان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushūʿ and khudūʿ are a heart's softness toward truth; hardness is its thickening against accepting truth.
rows.anchor: والخشوع والخضوع: لين القلب: للحق، وضده القسوة وهو غلظ القلب عن قبول الحق

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Ghayth may mean a cloud or, in Abu Ali's view, rain.
rows.anchor: كمثل غيث أي: سحاب، وقيل: مطر، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison may be to vegetation struck by rain that delights farmers with its beauty, or to disbelievers who attach themselves to worldly display, unlike believers who prefer the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كمثل نبات أصابه غيث أعجب الكفار الزراع نباته من حسنه، وقيل: بل المراد به الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant dries, yellows after being green, then breaks into chaff that displeases the eye after first delighting it.
rows.anchor: ثم يهيج أي: ييبس فتراه مصفرا من يبسه بعد خضرته ثم يكون حطاما منكسرا متفتتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife brings severe punishment to the persistent and forgiveness and divine pleasure to believers and penitents.
rows.anchor: وفي الآخرة عذاب شديد للمصرين ومغفرة من الله ورضوان للمؤمنين والتائبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is deceptive enjoyment because its attractive appearance conceals an opposite inner reality and outcome; the phrase also means people's work in gathering and acquiring it.
rows.anchor: لأنه يغتر بها لما يرى من حسن ظاهرها إذا لم يتفكر في عاقبتها، وخلاف باطنها لظاهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call asking whether it is time establishes proof and removes excuses, refuting determinists on human acts, capacity, and will.
rows.anchor: يدل قوله: (ألم يأن) الآية. على لزوم الحجة وإزاحة العلة، فيبطل قول المجبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites and disbelievers fear people more because they know little of God, His promises, and His warnings.
rows.anchor:
ووعده ووعيده.
ومنها: خذلان الله لهم، وإلقاء الرعب في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God abandons them and places fear in their hearts.
rows.anchor: خذلان الله لهم، وإلقاء الرعب في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the consequence of their affair shows that the affair was their act and they deserved its result, against determinism.
rows.anchor: دلالة قوله: وبال أمرهم أن ذلك الأمر فعلهم، واستحقوا جزاءه، خلاف قول المجبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeness may be the hypocrites' promises to Banu Nadir, like Satan's deceptive promise to a human who needs him.
rows.anchor: مثل المنافقين في وعدهم لبني النضير مثل الشيطان في وعده الإنسان بالغرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view compares the parable to Satan urging war at Badr, then retreating when he saw the angels and saying that he feared God.
rows.anchor: كمثل الشيطان يوم بدر دعا إلى حرب رسول الله، فلما رأى الملائكة رجع القهقرى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Satan and the human may be generic types: Satan continually calls people to disbelief, then disowns them when they need him.
rows.anchor: أراد بالشيطان والإنسان الجنس لا المعهود، وإنه عام، فإنه أبدا يدعوه إلى الكفر، ثم تبرأ منه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: A report identifies the human as the monk Barsisa, whom Satan induced to bow; the commentator rejects most of its implausible details but allows that the monk fornicated, killed the woman, was exposed, and crucified.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، وابن عباس. وفيه قصة طويلة لا يصح أكثرها، فتركت ذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the direct address, Satan tells a monotheist that monotheism is worthless and prophecy fabricated; the person accepts the call to disbelief.
rows.anchor: للموحد: التوحيد ليس بشيء، والنبوة مخرقة، فيقبل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's statement that he fears God may be mere pretense, spoken at the Resurrection, or spoken at Badr on seeing the angels.
rows.anchor: قيل: إنه يقولها تصنعا [وتعلقا] لا تحقيقا. وقيل: يقولها يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result is that Satan and the human both remain in Hell, the recompense of wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: فكان عاقبتهما يعني عاقبة الشيطان والإنسان أنهما في النار خالدين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God-consciousness means protecting oneself from punishment by performing obligations and avoiding sins.
rows.anchor: اتقوا الله أي: اتقوا عذابه بأداء الواجبات، واجتناب المعاصي

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: They interpret tomorrow as the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قيل: ليوم القيامة، عن قتادة، والضحاك، وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to be mindful may concern future conduct followed by repentance for past conduct, may be emphasis, or may address everyone first and then direct each person to self-examination.
rows.anchor: وكرر الأمر بالتقوى في المستقبل، والثاني بالتوبة عما سلف في الماضي، وقيل: تأكيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking ahead means taking account of oneself and what one has prepared for the gathering; calling the Resurrection tomorrow signals its nearness, as Qatada says.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأمر بالنظر: أمر بمحاسبة نفسه، وما الذي قدم ليوم حشره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting God may mean abandoning remembrance and being forsaken until one is treated as forgotten with respect to reward.
rows.anchor: تركوا ذكر الله فأنساهم بأن خذلهم حتى صاروا كالمنسي في حال استحقاق الثواب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Another reading is that they abandoned remembrance and were made to forget themselves through punishment that makes them forget one another, as in the instruction to greet one another.
rows.anchor: نسوا الله بترك ذكره، فأنساهم أنفسهم بالعذاب الذي ينسى بعضهم بعضا لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are forgetting God's teachings and failing to consider one's end, or forgetting one's own share in preparing good deeds; God does not grant them favor but abandons them.
rows.anchor: نسوا علوم الله حتى أنساه ذلك نفسه، فلم يتفكر في مصائره، وشر عواقبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inhabitants of the Fire and the Garden do not share the same condition: one group is in torment and the other has attained salvation and its desire.
rows.anchor: لا سواء حالهما، فأحدهما في النعيم، والآخر في الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that Satan entices through deception and then disowns the person, so that temptation is not created by God.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على أن الشيطان يوسوس بالغرور، ثم يتبرأ منه، فتدل على أن تلك الوسوسة والغرور ليس بخلق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse requires reflection, self-accounting, and preparation for the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوب التفكر في أمره، ومحاسبة نفسه، والاستعداد ليوم حشره

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads fa-aṣaddaq wa-akūn with a waw and open nūn as a response to the wish or question introduced by fa; he says the waw was omitted from the codex for brevity.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو: فأصدق وأكون بالواو وفتح النون على جواب التمني والاستفهام بالفاء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ reports seeing a form in some of Ibn Masud's codices, while Ubayy's and Ibn Masud's recitation is also reported with wa-akūn.
rows.anchor: وروي أن في حرف أبي وابن مسعود: (وأكون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use wa-akun in the jussive, coordinated to the underlying position of fa-aṣaddaq before fa; it could also be parsed as a response to the command.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: (وأكن) بالجزم عطفا بها على قوله: فأصدق

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the jussive because the written codices omit waw, most readers use it, and coordination to the pre-fa subjunctive is grammatically sound; a cited line supports this syntax.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد الجزم لثلاثة أوجه: أحدها: أنه يحذف الواو في مصحف عثمان

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ reports a form in some of Abdullah ibn Masud's codices.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: ورأيت في بعض مصاحف عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: The poet's line uses alhā to mean distracted or diverted from an affair.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: ألهى بني جشم عن كل مكرمة ... قصيدة قالها عمرو بن كلثوم

rows.speaker: كعب بن زهير
rows.claim: Kaʿb's line uses lā ulhiyannaka to mean I will not distract you, despite being occupied elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب بن زهير: وقال كل خليل كنت آمله ... لا ألهينك إني عنك مشغول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything that occupies someone and makes them neglect another matter has distracted them; wealth is named as the cause, as in expressions where an effect is attributed to its cause.
rows.anchor: كل شيء شغلك عن شيء فقد ألهاك عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term ajal means a period or fixed term, while ājil is the opposite of immediate.
rows.anchor: والأجل: الوقت ومدة الشيء، والآجل: ضد العاجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥadakum is accusative as the object of the verb yāti, although death is what comes; fa-aṣaddaq is subjunctive after a wish or question introduced by fa.
rows.anchor: أحدكم نصب بوقوع الفعل عليه وهو الموت، وإن تأخر. ونصب (فأصدق) لأنه جواب التمني بالفاء

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معدي كرب
rows.claim: His line illustrates a subjunctive verb after an imperative: leave me so I may go aside alone.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن معدي كرب: ذزني فأذهب جانبا ... وحدي وأكفك جانبي

rows.speaker: مقاتل وجماعة
rows.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about hypocrites; the address calls them believers outwardly, and ṣāliḥīn means sincere believers.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآية في المنافقين، عن مقاتل وجماعة. والمراد بقوله: (ياأيها الذين آمنوا) ظاهرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة
rows.claim: Another report places the revelation among believers and takes ṣāliḥīn to mean righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في المؤمنين، وأراد (بالصالحين) أي: بالأعمال الصالحة، عن ابن عباس وجماعة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Dhikr of God here most aptly means all forms of obedience.
rows.anchor: قيل: أراد بذكر الله جميع طاعاته، وهو قول أبي مسلم وهو الوجه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Another view restricts remembrance to the five daily prayers; other views take it as remembrance at all times or gratitude, patience, and acceptance in every condition.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد الصلوات الخمس، عن أبي علي، وقيل: ذكر الله على كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should not neglect God in hardship or blessing, since His beneficence continues in every condition.
rows.anchor: لا ينبغي أن يغفل في حال عن ذكر الله بؤسا كان أو نعمة، فإن إحسانه في جميع الحالات لا ينقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those distracted lose God's reward and mercy.
rows.anchor: خسروا ثواب الله ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending is explained as spending in jihad or in charitable causes, including zakat and all other obligatory dues.
rows.anchor: قيل: في الجهاد، وقيل: في سبيل البر، ويدخل فيه الزكوات وسائر الحقوق الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person asks for a brief extension after seeing signs of the afterlife, hoping to make up what was neglected.
rows.anchor: وذلك إذا عاين علامات الآخرة سأل الرجعة ليتدارك الغائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawlā may be an extra particle expressing a wish for delay or may mean halā as an interrogative request for more time.
rows.anchor: قيل: (لا) صلة والكلام على وجه التمني، وتقديره: لو أخرتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No warning against neglecting God's due is stronger than this passage.
rows.anchor: قيل: ليس في الزجر عن التفريط في حقوق الله آية أعظم من هذه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: For the view that the verse concerns hypocrites, the requested righteous standing means being among sincere believers.
rows.anchor: قيل: من المؤمنين المخلصين، والآية في المنافقين، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: For the view that it concerns believers, ṣāliḥīn means those obedient to God; Ibn Abbas also says a person who dies able to perform Hajj but has not done so, or has not paid zakat, will ask to return.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من المطيعين لله، والآية في المؤمنين، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas challenged those who said only disbelievers seek return after death, citing this verse about a person who failed to pay zakat or perform able-bodied Hajj.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: يا ابن عباس، اتق الله فإنما الكافر يسأل الرجعة! فقال: أنا أقرأ عليكم به قرآنا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that anyone dying without Hajj or zakat wishes for a short reprieve, but the request is denied.
rows.anchor: لا ينزل بأحد الموت ولم يحج ولا أدى زكاة إلا تمنى الرجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lifespans are recorded and neither advance nor recede; people should not rely on extra time after neglect, since they waste much time and then wish for a little more.
rows.anchor: يعني أعمار الخلق مكتوبة فلا تتقدم ولا تتأخر، فالواجب ألا يتكل المرء في تلافي ما فاته على عمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the dead were returned while compelled to know the truth, they could not be returned because they would be coerced; without compulsion, they would be like someone waking and resume their former ways, as 6:28 says.
rows.anchor: إذا اضطروا إلى المعرفة لا تجوز الإعادة؛ لأنهم يكونون ملجئين، وإن لم يكن كذلك فهو بمنزلة الانتباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their deeds and will recompense them for them.
rows.anchor: والله خبير بما تعملون أي: عليم بأعمالكم يجازلكم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to let wealth distract people shows that their acts originate from them; otherwise it would be God distracting them, and the text also says they are the losers.
rows.anchor: أفعال العباد حادثة من جهتهم؛ لأنها لو كانت مخلوقة لله تعالى لكان الله يلهيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to spend shows that wealth carries a due that must be paid before regret comes.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وأنفقوا) أن في المال حقا يجب إخراجه قبل حصول الحسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision cannot be unlawful, since spending from unlawful wealth is forbidden.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الرزق لا يكون حراما؛ لأن الإنفاق من الحرام محظور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request to return so they can give charity shows their acts belong to them; otherwise the request would make no sense, and they are capable of doing them.
rows.anchor: لأنها لو كانت خلقا له تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God will not delay anyone's term indicates that each person has one appointed lifespan, whether death occurs naturally or by killing.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (ولن يؤخر) الآية أن الأجل واحد؛ لأنه لا يتقدم ولا يتأخر

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub reads najmaʿukum with first-person plural, aligning it with the first-person verb anzalnā.
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب: نجمعكم بالنون اعتبارا بقوله: أنزلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the third-person verb yajmaʿukum, referring to God's name.
rows.anchor: الباقون بالياء كناية عن اسم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read nukaffir and nudkhil with first-person plural; the remaining readers use third-person forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر: نكفر، وندخله بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghubn is loss or shortchanging; taghābun is mutual loss, originally used of buying and selling when something is taken below its value.
rows.anchor: أصل الغبن النقص، والتغابن: تفاعل من الغبن، وذلك يكون بين اثنين، ويجري في البيع والشراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who trades the afterlife for the world is cheated by taking something trivial in exchange for something precious; the people of Hell are cheated by Paradise's people.
rows.anchor: ومن يشري الدنيا بالآخرة فهو بهذه الصفة؛ لأنهم أخذوا حقيرا، وأعطوا خطيرا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: An alternative etymology connects ghubn with concealing something, as in the hidden recesses called maghābin.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أصله من إخفاء الشيء، ومنه المغابن: المواضع التي تخفى، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm may be accusative as a time expression, or as an exhortation to remember the day and prepare for it.
rows.anchor: يوم قيل: نصب على الظرف، أي: يبعثون يوم، وقيل: نصب على الإغراء، أي: اذكروا يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In bi-annahu, the hāʾ may be an expletive support or a pronoun referring to firmness.
rows.anchor: قيل: الهاء عماد، وقيل: كناية عن الثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment came because messengers brought clear proofs, arguments, and miracles, but people denied them and turned away; God needs neither them nor their worship and only commands for their benefit.
rows.anchor: ذلك العذاب نزل بهم لأجل أن الرسل أتتهم بالبينات والحجج والمعجزات فأنكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is described as self-sufficient and praiseworthy: either praised, or deserving praise for blessing people despite their disbelief.
rows.anchor: والله غني لا تجوز عليه الحاجة حميد قيل: محمود، وقيل: من حقه أن يحمد لإنعامه عليهم مع كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath confirms resurrection; the resurrected will either be shown their deeds written in records or informed of them and recompensed, and reviving all creation is easy for God in an instant.
rows.anchor: ذكر القسم تأكيدا للبعث ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم قيل: لتخبرن بأن يعرض عليهم مكتوبا في الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light sent down is identified as the Qur'an, which illuminates religious matters and guides people.
rows.anchor: والنور الذي أنزلنا قيل: هو القرآن؛ لأنه ينور أمر الدين، وبه يهتدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may gather people from their graves toward Judgment, or gather them on Judgment Day because all creatures assemble there.
rows.anchor: قيل: يجمعكم من القبور ليوم القيامة، أي: يميتكم جميعا، وقيل: يجمعكم في يوم الجمع يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: One interpretation says the people of Paradise cheat the people of Hell by winning the good outcome.
rows.anchor: قيل: غبن أهل الجنة أهل النار، عن قتادة، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the people of Hell lose by choosing transient worldly life and thereby forfeiting the far more valuable reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل: غبن أهل النار؛ لما نالهم من العذاب بإيثارهم الدنيا الفانية

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a Prophetic report that each believer entering Paradise is shown the Hell seat they would have occupied by wrongdoing, while each person entering Hell is shown the Paradise seat they would have had by doing good, increasing gratitude or regret.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في تفسيرها: ما من عبد مؤمن يدخل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view is that people in Paradise outdo one another in the increase of their ranks.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يغبن أهل الجنة بعضهم بعضا في زيادة الدرجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God erases the sins of believers who do good, admits them to gardens with rivers, and grants them eternal residence; this is great success, attaining what is sought and escaping harm.
rows.anchor: يكفر عنه سيئاته أي: معاصيه ويدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers denied God's signs, meaning the proofs and Qur'an, and their destination is the Fire.
rows.anchor: وكذبوا بآياتنا بالحجج والقرآن أولئك أصحاب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that punishment came because of their deeds shows that punishment is deserved for sins, which are their own acts.
rows.anchor: أن العقاب يستحق على المعاصي، وأن المعاصي فعلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By asking whether ordinary humans could guide them, the people showed their inability to answer the manifest miracle and shifted to an irrelevant objection; prophethood concerns benefit, not shared species.
rows.anchor: عجزوا عند ظهور المعجزة، فعدلوا إلى ما ليس بحجة؛ لأن الرسالة لا تتعلق بالجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creation is gathered at Judgment, hence the name Day of Gathering; it is called Mutual Loss because the people of Hell forfeit Paradise's reward and enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: أن جميع الخلق يحشر يوم القيامة، لذلك سمي يوم الجمع، وسمي التغابن لعظم ما يجري من الغبن

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The verse indicates that human acts originate with people; if God created them, mutual loss would not make sense, just as it would not for bodily forms.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن أفعال العباد حادثة من جهتهم؛ إذ لو كان خلقا لله لما صح التغابن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has ḍamma on wajdikum, while Yaqub uses kasra and al-Araj fatḥa; all three are valid dialect forms.
rows.anchor: قراءة. القراء: وجدكم بضم الواو، وعن يعقوب بكسرها، وعن الأعرج بفتحها، وكلها لغات صحيحة

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Related vowel patterns distinguish finding a lost object, grief, or anger; al-wajd in this verse is the means a person possesses.
rows.anchor: ووجدت الضالة وجدانا، ووجدت من الحزن وجدا، ومن الغضب موجدة ووجدانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit records the three vowel patterns for finding or having means, while related patterns distinguish finding a lost object, grief, or anger; al-wajd in this verse is the means a person possesses.
rows.anchor: حكاها ابن السكيت يقال: وجدت في المال وجدا ووجدا ووجدا، بتعاقب الحركات الثلاث على الواو

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jafar reads ka-ayyin lightly without hamza.
rows.anchor: كاين بوزن كاهن خفيفة بغير همز قرأها أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads kāʾin with hamza on the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأها ابن كثير بوزن كاهن مهموزة الياء في (كائن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers double the yāʾ in kaʾayyin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون مشددة على وزن كعين

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read nukran with a silent kāf; the common form is reported from Hafs and Ismail from Asim, and the other readers use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي: نكرا ساكنة الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iskān is giving someone a place to dwell, from the root for stillness.
rows.anchor: الإسكان: أن يسكنه موضعا، يقال: أسكنت داره، وأصله من السكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḍārra means constriction, crowding, and inflicting harm on each other; ḍarūra is being driven into the narrowest circumstances.
rows.anchor: والمضارة: المضايقة والمزاحمة، وهو إلحاق الضرر بكل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An imperative is literally a verbal command; applying it to an action or condition is figurative, while iʾtimār can mean commanding one another, complying with a command, or acting on one's own initiative.
rows.anchor: والأمر في القول حقيقة، وفي الفعل مجاز، يقال: أمره مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imr, with kasra on hamza, means a remarkable or wondrous thing.
rows.anchor: والإمر بكسر الهمز: العجب

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع والحسن وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read yubaddilnā with fatḥa and a doubled dāl, also using the form yubaddiluhu in al-Tahrim.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع والحسن وأبو عمرو: يبدلنا بفتح الباء وتشديد الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the light form yubdilnā with a silent bāʾ and undoubled dāl; both are valid forms.
rows.anchor: الباقون ساكنة الباء خفيفة الدال، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinguish the forms: tabdīl changes an item's state while the entity remains, whereas ibdāl removes one thing and puts another in its place.
rows.anchor: فالتبديل: تغيير الشيء بتغير حاله وعينه قائم، والإبدال: رفع الشيء، ووضع شيء آخر مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trial, testing, and examination are synonyms; God's trial is the imposition of duties so acts occur and become manifest, although He knew beforehand they would occur, so testing is figurative of His treatment of the tested person.
rows.anchor: والابتلاء من الله هو التعبد والتكليف، فكلفهم ليظهر من أعمالهم، فيعلم الله تعالى وقوعها كما علم من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarm is cutting, especially harvesting date fruit; ṣarām and jadhādh name the harvest, and the separation between companions is also called ṣarm.
rows.anchor: والصرم: أصله: القطع، والصرام والجذاذ: قطع ثمر النخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both dawn and night are called ṣarīm because each cuts off the one before it; aṣbaḥa means to enter the morning.
rows.anchor: ويقال للصبح: صريم، والليل: صريم؛ لأن كل واحد يقطع عن صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exception removes a member from a general class; an exception by God's will instead lifts the ruling of the statement, such as saying unless God wills to prevent or enable me.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء: إخراج بعض من كل، لولاه لدخل فيه

rows.speaker: أبو العالية ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: They take ḥardin as purposeful seriousness and exertion in what the owners intended.
rows.anchor: على جد وجهد من أمرهم، عن أبي العالية، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وابن زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan explains ḥardin as the strain of poverty.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على جهد من الفاقة، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan takes ḥardin to mean anger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على حنق، عن سفيان، أي: غضب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والقتبي
rows.claim: They understand it as firm intent to withhold, supported by idioms for a year withholding rain and camels withholding milk.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على جد في المنع، عن أبي عبيدة، و[القتبي]

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة والقرظي والنخعي
rows.claim: They interpret it as a matter resolved by common agreement.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على أمر مجمع بينهم، عن مجاهد، وعكرمة، والقرظي، والنخعي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they thought themselves powerful and able.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على قوة وقدرة قادرين عند أنفسهم، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes it as setting out purposefully, from the idiom ḥarada ḥardahu, to aim at his aim.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على قصد، أي: خرجوا قاصدين مجدين فيما عزموا عليه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says ḥard is the name of the garden, but the commentator judges this explanation unsound.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الحرد: اسم الجنة، عن السدي، وليس بالوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qādirīn may mean that they thought they could keep the poor away, or that they expected to reach the garden at their chosen harvest time; the latter is Abu Muslim's view.
rows.anchor: قادرين قيل: قادرين عند أنفسهم على منعهم، وقيل: قادرين على موافاتهم الجنة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: When they saw the garden, they thought they had lost the way and this could not be their orchard.
rows.anchor: قيل: [ضللنا] الطريق فليس هذا بستاننا، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations are that they had strayed from the truth and were punished for their conduct, or had strayed by withholding the poor's due.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضالون عن الحق في أمرنا؛ فلذلك عوقبنا بذهاب ثمرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They realize this is their garden but have been deprived of its benefit because they denied the needy their due and failed to make an exception.
rows.anchor: بل نحن محرومون يعني هذه جنتنا، ولكن حرمنا نفعها وخيرها لمنع المساكين حقهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: They interpret awsaṭuhum as the most just in speech.
rows.anchor: قال أوسطهم قيل: أعدلهم مقالة، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other possibilities are the best and wisest, the person nearest to what is best, or the oldest among them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أفضلهم وأعقلهم، والأوسط: الأقرب إلى الأصلح

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Lā tusabbiḥūn may mean why did you not make an exception, since doing so expresses trust in God and disavowal of one's own power.
rows.anchor: لولا تسبحون أي: لولا تستثنون، عن مجاهد؛ لأن في الاستثناء التوكل على الله

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: They used subḥānallāh as their formula for making an exception.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان استثناؤهم سبحان الله، عن أبي صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings urge them to glorify and remember God, thank Him for His gifts, ask His forgiveness, and return the matter to His will rather than counsel one another to deny the poor their due; the latter is Abu Muslim's explanation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هلا تسبحون الله، وتذكرونه، وتشكرونه على ما أعطاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is to declare God free of injustice, since He does not wrong people and does not approve their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: هلا نزهتم الله عن الظلم، فإنه لا يظلم، ولا يرضى منكم بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause may rebuke them, followed by a fresh exhortation to glorify God and return to Him.
rows.anchor: قوله: (ألم أقل لكم) تقريع، وقوله: (لولا تسبحون) ابتداء حث على التسبيح لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their declaration that God is exalted means He did not wrong them; their own injustice lay in deciding to deny the poor their due.
rows.anchor: في عزمنا حرمان المساكين حقوقهم، يعني هو منزه عن الظلم فما فعل بنا لم يكن ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They blamed one another for their own failures.
rows.anchor: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتلاومون أي: يلوم بعضهم بعضا على ما فرط منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit exceeding the limits in withholding the poor's share and failing to make an exception; another view says they failed to thank God and follow their fathers' good example.
rows.anchor: إنا كنا طاغين أي: مجاوزين للحد في منع الفقراء حقهم وترك الاستثناء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report says that after they sincerely repented, God replaced their garden with another called al-Ḥayawān, whose grape cluster was so large a mule could carry it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما أخلصوا أبدلهم الله بها جنة، يقال لها: الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owners are blamed for denying the poor their due, swearing to do so, and omitting an exception; this supports requiring an exception when speaking about the future, since one cannot be sure the statement will come true.
rows.anchor: ذمهم على منع الحق، وذمهم على القسم عليه، وذمهم على ترك الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intending an evil act is itself blameworthy: they were punished for the resolve even before committing the wrong, and actually taking property and denying rights is worse.
rows.anchor: أن العزم على القبيح قبيح؛ لأنهم عوقبوا على عزمهم من غير منع وظلم بالمنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loss of the fruit may have been punishment or a trial that served as a grace, since it led them to repent.
rows.anchor: يجوز الوجهان: أن يكون عقوبة، وأن يكون لطفا؛ لذلك تابوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor had an enforceable due in the harvest, variously identified as a tenth or as the fruit that fell during picking.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في ذلك الحق، فقيل: كان حقهم العشر، وقيل: بل ما كان يتساقط من الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling one of the brothers their middlemost indicates that he was a believer who enjoined right conduct.
rows.anchor: يدل قوله: (قال أوسطهم) أنه كان مؤمنا يأمر بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their admission that they had been unjust shows injustice is an act of the servant.
rows.anchor: دلالة قوله: (إنا كنا ظالمين) أن الظلم فعل العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hope and turning toward God show they repented.
rows.anchor: ومنها: دلالة قوله: (إنا إلى ربنا راغبون) أنهم تابوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After sin, a servant should turn back to God; Hasan advised against fighting al-Hajjaj with the sword and urged repentance and prayer, since God would not grant victory while people persisted in sin.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن الحسن أنه قيل له: ألا تخرج على الحجاج؟ فقال: هو عقوبة من الله فلا تقاتلوه بالسيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should not be occupied with accumulating wealth; wealth carries a due, and withholding it brings a threat of punishment.
rows.anchor: أنه لا ينبغي أن يشتغل بجمع المال. ومنها: أن في المال حقا يلحقه الوعيد بمنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away, retreating, and gathering wealth are acts of the servant, which is why the servant deserves punishment.
rows.anchor: أن الإدبار والتولي والجمع فعل العبد؛ لذلك استحق العذاب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the plural amānāt with no alif after the nūn; the remaining readers have the plural with alif.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: لأمانتهم بغير ألف بعد النون على واحدة

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read shahādātihim in the plural with alif after the dāl; other readers use the singular, and all read ṣalātihim in the singular.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم ويعقوب: بشهاداتهم بألف بعد الدال على الجمع

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Haluʿ is swift and agitated; Abu Muslim gives the example of a fast, light she-camel. Another explanation is extreme greed coupled with the worst anxiety.
rows.anchor: الهلوع: العجول الضجور، وناقة هلواع: إذا كانت سريعة خفيفة، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jazaʿ is the opposite of patience.
rows.anchor: والجزع: خلاف الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaqq is placing something where reason and sacred law call for it to be placed.
rows.anchor: والحق: وضع الشيء موضعه، على ما يدعو إليه العقل والشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿādī is one who goes beyond what is right; the term also derives from moving quickly out of the right way into injustice.
rows.anchor: والعادي: الخارج عن الحق عدا فهو عاد: إذا اعتدى

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Haluʿan is accusative as a circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: هلوعا نصب على الحال، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Jazūʿan and manūʿan are accusative by proximity to halūʿan, rather than in the same grammatical role as it.
rows.anchor: و جزوعا ومنوعا نصب على المجاورة لقوله: هلوعا ولم ينصب على ما نصب عليه هلوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haluʿ means greedy and impatient: the human is created desirous and hastens to satisfy desire with little patience, so must be taught patience and restraint; desire is necessary for moral responsibility.
rows.anchor: قيل: الهلوع الحريص الضجور، يعني خلق مشتهيا فهو يستبق إلى شهواته، ويقل صبره عنها

rows.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains haluʿ by the following traits: when afflicted by harm, one is anxious, and when given good, one withholds it.
rows.anchor: وإذا مسه الخير منوعا (21)، عن عطية عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says haluʿ means stingy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شحيحا، عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd explain it as being highly anxious.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جزوعا، عن قتادة، وابن زيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak say it means greedy and voracious.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حريصا شرها، عن مجاهد، والضحاك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets haluʿ as narrowness of heart.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ضيق القلب، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says God created people loving what pleases them and hating what hurts them, then commands them to give what they love and endure what they dislike.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خلقه الله تعالى يحب ما يسره ويرضيه ويكره ما يدهيه، ثم تعبده بإنفاق ما يحب

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata explains haluʿ as hasty.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عجولا، عن عطاء

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وثعلب
rows.claim: They say the person fails to give thanks when blessed and fails to be patient when afflicted.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة، وثعلب، وقيل: إذا أقتر جزع، وإذا أيسر منع

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl explains the traits as anxiety when poor and stinginess when prosperous.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إذا أقتر جزع، وإذا أيسر منع، عن سهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description may refer specifically to disbelievers or to all people; alternatively, humans are created weak in bearing these traits, not with the traits fully formed from infancy, but desirous, needy, and weak, which leads to impatience and withholding.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالكفار خاصة، وقيل: الخلق عامة، وقيل: خلق ضعيفا عن الصبر على الهلع والجزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uprightness may bring the reward of Paradise and may be a cause of expanded provision.
rows.anchor: أن الجنة تنال بالاستقامة، وأنها يجوز أن تكون سببا لسعة الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage requires reflection on proofs.
rows.anchor: ومنها: على وجوب التفكر في الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly work in mosques is disliked; scholars differ on judicial work, which Abu Hanifa permits as religious business while al-Shafiʿi regards it as disliked.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في القضاء، لا يكره عند أبي حنيفة؛ لأنها من أمور الدين، وقال الشافعي: يكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must detach himself and rely on God alone, as shown by saying he controls neither harm nor guidance.
rows.anchor: ومنها: وجوب الانقطاع إليه تعالى؛ لذلك قال: (لا أملك لكم ضرا ولا رشدا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about people nearly becoming a compact crowd around the Prophet could be praise or blame.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل قوله: (كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا) أن يكون مدحا وذما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uprightness is the servant's own act, not created by God, refuting determinists.
rows.anchor: أن الاستقامة فعل العبد، ليس بخلق الله تعالى، فيبطل قول المجبرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read liyaʿlama with passive voice, meaning that people will know the messengers delivered their Lord's messages.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس ويعقوب بضم الياء: ليعلم على ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the active form liyaʿlama.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They pronounce the yāʾ in rabbī with fatḥa; the remaining readers leave it quiescent.
rows.anchor: وفتح أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو الياء من قوله: ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijāra means protecting someone from harm reaching him; no one can protect against God because His power is complete.
rows.anchor: الإجارة: المنع من لحاق الشر به، أجار يجير إجارة فهو مجير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Multaḥad is a refuge reached by turning aside toward safety; its root refers to a path that veers from the straight line and also names the side niche of a grave.
rows.anchor: والملتحد: الملتجأ بالميل إلى جهة السلامة به، وهو مفتعل من اللحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants protection but cannot be protected against, since no one can prevent His will because His power is complete.
rows.anchor: والله يجير، ولا يجار عليه؛ لأنه لا يتهيأ لأحد أن يجير عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀlim al-ghayb may be an adjective of rabbī or a predicate with an omitted subject, meaning He is the knower of the unseen.
rows.anchor: عالم الغيب) رفع لأنه نعت لقوله: ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasluk can be intransitive or transitive; the source compares it with the Qur'anic expressions for water coursing as springs and for making roads through mountains.
rows.anchor: و (يسلك) لازم ومتعد، سلكه وأسلكه، ومنه: (فسلكه ينابيع)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raṣadan is accusative as an object, understood as a watchman God appoints and sends along the messenger's front and rear.
rows.anchor: رصدا نصب لأنه مفعول، كأنه قيل: يجعل رصدا نسلكه من بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdadan may be a circumstantial accusative or an accusative of verbal noun, meaning a counted enumeration.
rows.anchor: عددا نصب على الحال، وقيل: على المصدر، أي: عد عددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase moves from singular lahu to plural khālidīn because man can refer to a group.
rows.anchor: لأنه أخبر عن (من) و(من) تكون للجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When idolaters offered to protect the Prophet if he abandoned his message, revelation instructed him to say no one can protect against God, who has power by His own essence and cannot be restrained.
rows.anchor: قيل: إذ المشركين قالوا لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: إنك أتيت بأمر عظيم لم يسمع بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to explain that God alone owns benefit and harm and knows the unseen; the Messenger's duty is to convey the message.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر تعالى نبيه أن يبين لهم أن المالك النفع والضر، وعالم الغيب هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Multaḥad can mean a refuge or a helper; al-Kalbi explains it as an underground entrance and al-Suddi as a fortress.
rows.anchor: قيل: ملجأ أميل إليه، عن قتادة، وقيل: نصيرا، وقيل: مدخلا في الأرض مثل السرب

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو علي
rows.claim: Except for conveying God's message: this is the Prophet's refuge and means of salvation.
rows.anchor: إلا بلاغا من الله يعني تبليغا لرسالته فإنه ملجئي وملتحدي، وفيه لي الأمر والنجاة، عن الحسن، وأبي علي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Another reading is that the Prophet has no control over harm or guidance, only the ability to convey revelation with God's help.
rows.anchor: لا أملك لكم ضرا ولا رشدا، فما علي إلا البلاغ عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views say no one will protect the Prophet if he fails to deliver, while delivery makes God his protector; he is a messenger who holds only what God has given him.
rows.anchor: لا يجيرني من الله أحد إن لم أبلغ رسالته، وإن بلغت كان هو لي مجيرا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim allows the exception to mean what God has conveyed and given to the Prophet, with no refuge apart from what God commanded him.
rows.anchor: يحتمل (بلاغا) معنيين: أحدهما: إلا ما بلغني من الله وأتاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers put the conditional phrase after the object, while Ibn Masud and Atiyya move yawm before in khiftum; Abu al-Sammal uses kasra on the nūn in tattaqūna by annexation, but the agreed form has fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود وعطية: فكيف تتقون يوما يجعل الولدان شييبا إن كفرتم، وقرأ أبو [السمال] العدوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative dhar is formed from a future-only verb; its past is absent because the preferable verb taraka serves instead, and the initial wāw is avoided when paired with hamza, as in daʿ.
rows.anchor: لفظة (ذر) جاء مستقبلا، وأخذ منه الأمر والنهي، ولم يجئ منه الماضي استغناء عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿma has several senses: enjoyment, wealth, favor, delight when pronounced with ḍamma on the nūn, and property.
rows.anchor: والنعمة: التنعم، والنعمة: الثروة، والنعمة: المنة، والنعمة بضم النون: المسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamhīl means postponement or delay.
rows.anchor: والتمهيل: التأخير في المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankāl are shackles; the singular is nakal.
rows.anchor: والأنكال: القيود، واحدها نكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuṣṣa is a morsel stuck in the throat and impossible to swallow; a ghuṣṣa in the heart is pain so intense that food and drink cannot pass.
rows.anchor: والغصة: تزدد اللقمة في الفم، لا يسيغها آكلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kathīb is a large mass of gathered sand.
rows.anchor: والكثيب: الرمل المجتمع الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhīl is flowing sand; the entry gives related forms for shifting, pouring, and streaming sand, including the Prophetic instruction to measure rather than pour loosely.
rows.anchor: والمهيل: السائل، يقال: هلت الرمل أهيله: إذا حركت أسفله، فسال من أعلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wabīl means heavy and severe; its root conveys heaviness, and related words describe unpalatable fodder and heavy rain.
rows.anchor: والوبيل: الثقيل الشديد، وبناؤه فعيل من الوبال، وكل ثقيل وبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet describes the meal of Bajila and Malik's horsemen as wabīl, demonstrating the word's sense of a heavy meal.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: لقد أكلت بجيلة يوم لاقت ... فوارس مالك أكلا وبيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shiyāb is the plural of ashīb and means gray hair.
rows.anchor: والشيب: جمع أشيب، والشيب: بياض الشعر

rows.speaker: نافع وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read wa-l-layli idh with idh and no alif in the next word; the remaining readers use idhā. Both dabbara and adbara are valid forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب: والليل إذ بغير ألف وسكون. الذال، وقرأ الباقون: إذا بالألف

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim argues for idhā because Qur'anic oaths use idhā, not idh.
rows.anchor: قال [أبو حاتم]: ليس في القرآن قسم بجنبه (إذ)، ولكن الأقسام بجنبها إذا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers idhā because it parallels the following oath, waṣ-ṣubḥi idhā asfar.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: هو ليس موافقة للحرف الذي يليه؛ ألا ترى أنه قال: (والصبح إذا أسفر)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both recitations of idh and idhā are sound and evident; neither has priority over the other.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنهما قراءتان ظاهرتان ليس لأحدهما على الأخرى ترجيح

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim explains dabbara as coming immediately after daytime, the opposite of adbara, which means turning away and departing.
rows.anchor: دبر جاء بعد النهار، وفي دبر النهار، أي: أقبل عقيب النهار، وهذا ضد أدبر

rows.speaker: ابن السميقع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqa reads waṣ-ṣubḥ idh safara without alif; safara and asfara are both valid words for becoming bright, possibly from a woman uncovering her face.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن السميقع: إذا سفر بغير ألف وهما لغتان، سفر وجه فلان وأسفر: إذا أضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has naḏīran in the accusative, understood as a command to the wrapped Prophet to rise as a warner, or as a circumstantial expression attached to the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: نذيرا بالنصب، قيل: تقديره: يا أيها المدثر قم نذيرا للبشر

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim also parses naḏīran as an accusative of specification.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نصب على القطع، وقيل: على التمييز، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Abi Abla reads naḏīr in the nominative, meaning that it is a warner.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة: نذير بالرفع أي: هو نذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isfār means appearance and becoming visible; the cited verse uses sufūr for a woman's appearing without her veil.
rows.anchor: الإسفار: الظهور والبروز، قال الشاعر: وكنت إذا ما جئت ليلى تبرقعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kubar is the plural of kubrā, following the pattern of awlā/awwal and ukhrā/ukhar.
rows.anchor: والكبر: جمع كبرى، كما يقال: أولى وأول، وأخرى وأخر
